title: Cloud & Well-Architected Foundations
oneLiner: Learn how AWS is laid out globally and the design principles every SAA question is graded against.
examWeightNote: Foundational — not a scored domain, but the mental model behind every question.
objectives: Explain Regions, Availability Zones, and edge locations, and when to use each.
Describe the AWS shared responsibility model — what AWS secures vs what you secure.
Recall the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework.
Understand the global vs regional vs zonal scope of core services.

services.name: AWS Regions & AZs
services.purpose: Physically isolated geographic areas (Regions) each made of multiple data-center clusters (AZs) for fault isolation.

services.name: Edge Locations / CloudFront
services.purpose: Global points of presence that cache content close to users and terminate connections.

services.name: AWS IAM
services.purpose: Global service controlling who can do what across your account.

services.name: AWS Well-Architected Tool
services.purpose: Reviews workloads against the six-pillar framework.

keyConcepts: A Region is a collection of ≥3 Availability Zones; AZs are one or more discrete data centers with redundant power and networking.
Design across multiple AZs for high availability; design across multiple Regions for disaster recovery and lowest global latency.
Shared responsibility: AWS secures the cloud (hardware, global infra); you secure what's in the cloud (data, IAM, OS patching for EC2, config).
The six Well-Architected pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability.
Some services are global (IAM, Route 53, CloudFront, WAF), most are regional (EC2, S3 buckets live in a Region), and a few are zonal (EC2 instances, EBS volumes).

scenarios.scenario: A startup runs its entire app on EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone. During a power event in that AZ, the app went fully offline for hours.
scenarios.question: What is the simplest change to prevent a single-AZ outage from taking the whole app down?

options.label: Move all instances to a larger instance type
Deploy instances across at least two AZs behind a load balancer
Enable Amazon CloudFront in front of the instances
Buy Reserved Instances for cost savings

scenarios.explanation: High availability comes from spreading compute across multiple AZs behind a load balancer, so one AZ failing doesn't take the app offline. A bigger instance or CloudFront doesn't add AZ-level fault tolerance.

scenarios.scenario: Your compliance team asks who is responsible for applying security patches to the guest operating system on your EC2 instances.
scenarios.question: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, who patches the guest OS on EC2?
scenarios.explanation: With EC2 (IaaS), the customer is responsible for the guest OS, including patching, plus applications and data. AWS is responsible for the underlying hardware and hypervisor. (Managed services like Fargate/Lambda shift more of this to AWS.)

quiz.question: What is an AWS Availability Zone?
options: One or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity within a Region
A global cache of content near users
A billing boundary for an AWS account
quiz.answer: One or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity within a Region
quiz.explanation: An AZ is one or more discrete data centers with independent power/cooling/networking. Multiple AZs make up a Region and let you build fault-tolerant architectures.

quiz.question: Which of these is a GLOBAL AWS service (not scoped to a single Region)?
quiz.explanation: IAM is global — users, roles, and policies apply account-wide. EC2, EBS, and RDS are regional/zonal resources.

quiz.question: You want to protect against an entire Region becoming unavailable. What should you design for?
quiz.explanation: Multi-AZ protects against AZ failure. To survive a whole-Region outage (disaster recovery) you replicate across Regions.

quiz.question: Which pillar is NOT one of the six AWS Well-Architected Framework pillars?
quiz.explanation: The six pillars are Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability. 'Marketability' is not a pillar.

quiz.question: Under the shared responsibility model, which is AWS's responsibility?
options: Physical security of the data centers
quiz.answer: Physical security of the data centers
quiz.explanation: AWS is responsible for 'security OF the cloud' — the physical facilities, hardware, and global infrastructure. Customers handle 'security IN the cloud' such as IAM, encryption choices, and security-group rules.

quiz.question: What are AWS edge locations used for?
options: Caching and delivering content close to users to reduce latency
quiz.answer: Caching and delivering content close to users to reduce latency
quiz.explanation: Edge locations are part of the CloudFront/global network — they cache content and terminate connections near users, lowering latency. They are separate from Regions and AZs.

quiz.question: Multi-AZ deployments primarily protect against which type of failure?
options: A single data center or AZ becoming unavailable
quiz.answer: A single data center or AZ becoming unavailable
quiz.explanation: Multiple AZs give high availability within a Region — one AZ can fail without taking your app down. Surviving a whole-Region outage requires a multi-Region (DR) design.

quiz.question: Which of the following is the CUSTOMER's responsibility under the shared responsibility model?
options: Configuring IAM permissions and encrypting their data
quiz.answer: Configuring IAM permissions and encrypting their data
quiz.explanation: Customers own 'security IN the cloud' — IAM configuration, data encryption choices, network/security-group rules, and (for EC2) the guest OS. AWS secures the underlying infrastructure.

quiz.question: How many Availability Zones does an AWS Region typically contain at minimum?
quiz.explanation: AWS Regions are designed with at least three (often more) Availability Zones so customers can build highly available, fault-tolerant architectures.

quiz.question: Which Well-Architected pillar focuses on running and monitoring systems and continuously improving processes?
quiz.explanation: Operational Excellence covers running, monitoring, and improving workloads and procedures. The other pillars target cost, performance, security, reliability, and sustainability respectively.
